description:
Proposal page (approved 2026-11-07): https://claude.ai/artifact/Wx4cwENxiEe7qPfqni84ZN

A send runs the receiver's matcher on the sender against the sender's own message, copies only what the pattern binds (hit) or the message (miss) into a detached segment of the sender's own heap chain, and gifts that segment to the receiver through its in-queue under the receiver's queue lock. The receiver grafts the segment with pointer moves; the next Cheney pass treats it as from-space. No process ever writes into another process's live heap. Self-send is a mailbox push; the compiler's call-site publication of possibly-aliased arguments (construct_call_ownership) already keeps the message intact, so the runtime copies and publishes nothing.

Base: fz-sc8.66/scheduling-core @ 0163a8805 (PR #276). Work happens on one branch in worktree ../fz-gift and lands as one PR stacked on #276; each child ticket is one commit pushed to that PR as it closes.

Decisions taken from the proposal's open list: tip adoption on graft is not built; the interpreter path is in scope for parity on every step. The decision to start a gift at the smallest size class and chain upward was measured and is reversed by fz-a9y.11 (measure first, one block).

Not in scope: multi-worker scheduling itself, receive markers, an off-heap message mode, the BEAM direct-on-heap try-lock fast path.

## Phase 2: the heap fold (2026-11-08)

Tickets .1 to .7 landed on PR #279 (head 71ac1ebbb, CI green). Reviewing the result against BEAM's collector (erl_gc.c, erl_message.c in the local checkout ../otp) showed that the gift epic had added a second instance of a pre-existing defect and that several heap mechanisms are more complicated than the problem they solve:

- Two accountings disagree. The pressure flag is raised from own + adopted + fragment bytes; the band decision reconstructs the trigger from own bytes alone. A non-pressured collection can size to-space below live data and panic. Reachable through gifts alone (probe attached to .9).
- Adopted blocks are abandoned blocks with a second identity (fill vs capacity, in or out of the band decision).
- Oversize objects run a mark-sweep collector inside the copying collector because the size table clamps at 32 entries.
- A gift starts at 1 KiB and overflows, so the window snapshots and splits lists; BEAM measures first and allocates once.
- Six public collect entries and three root-set assemblies; BEAM has one setup_rootset.
- quiet_quanta is written and never read; a gift's dtor list is empty by construction; freelist_len is a constant.

BEAM's shape, adopted here: one counter for everything outside the tip, a collect-now predicate over state, to-space sized from copyable bytes before any policy, an unbounded size table. Kept on purpose: single-decision sizing (a second resize costs a second Cheney here), the thread-local block pool, deferred dtors (fz code, not C).

Order: .8 deletes scaffolding, .9 fixes the accounting and the panic, .10 deletes fragments, .11 measures gifts, .12 unifies the root set, .13 closes out docs and the PR. Chained for one builder in ../fz-gift.
title: Gift-heap send: a sender matches in place and gifts a heap segment the receiver grafts
